sec: Work-up flow of portal HTN and the HVPG measurement · p1003

items.q: In the p1003 work-up flow, the step ‘Deranged LFT + USG : fatty liver + negative serology’ is qualified by:
items.exp: Flow: deranged LFT + USG : fatty liver + negative serology (AST / ALT < 150) → confirms chronic hepatitis (NASH). (Book p1003)

items.q: The Fibroscan value in the p1003 flow that leads to the diagnosis of cirrhosis is:
items.exp: Flow: confirms chronic hepatitis (NASH) → Fibroscan : 13.5 kPa → cirrhosis. (Book p1003)

items.q: After cirrhosis is established in the flow, the pair of findings that establishes portal hypertension (+) is:
items.exp: Flow: cirrhosis → splenomegaly (+), ↓ platelet → portal hypertension (+). (Book p1003)

items.q: Portal HTN is quantified with HVPG, where:
items.exp: Quantity with HVPG: HVPG = WHVP − FHVP. (Book p1003)

items.q: Match the p1003 abbreviations — 1) HVPG  2) WHVP  3) FHVP … A) Wedged hepatic venous pressure  B) Free hepatic venous pressure  C) Hepatic venous pressure gradient
items.exp: HVPG : hepatic venous pressure gradient; WHVP : wedged hepatic venous pressure; FHVP : free hepatic venous pressure. (Book p1003)

items.q: ‘On p1003 the expansion line prints the free pressure as “FWVP : Free hepatic venous pressure”, while the formula line prints HVPG = WHVP − FHVP.’
opts: True — the two printings differ (FWVP vs FHVP)
False — the formula line prints FWVP
True, but the values are different concepts
items.exp: The expansion line is printed ‘FWVP : Free hepatic venous pressure’ whereas the formula is ‘HVPG = WHVP − FHVP’; both denote the free hepatic venous pressure. (Book p1003)

items.q: A child with EHPVO has large oesophageal varices but a normal HVPG. Which row of the p1003 table explains why HVPG fails here?
opts: Prehepatic row — WHVP, FHVP and HVPG all normal
Postsinusoidal row — WHVP increased, FHVP normal
items.exp: Prehepatic: normal / normal / normal — the gradient across the liver is normal because the obstruction is before the liver. (Book p1003)

items.q: ‘In the p1003 flow, portal hypertension (+) is established only by endoscopy.’
opts: False — it follows cirrhosis with splenomegaly (+) and ↓ platelet; endoscopy is one of two follow-up arms
True — endoscopy is the sole step that establishes portal hypertension (+)
False — Fibroscan 13.5 kPa alone establishes the diagnosis of portal hypertension
True, but only when the HVPG arm is not performed in the same session
items.exp: Flow: cirrhosis → splenomegaly (+), ↓ platelet → portal hypertension (+), which then branches to quantity with HVPG and endoscopy. (Book p1003)
